# Sirach Chapter 22 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 22 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**Council Notes:**
Chapter 22 divides into three movements: the sluggard (vv. 1-2), the fool and foolish/shameless daughters (vv. 3-18), and friendship tested by trouble (vv. 19-27). The chapter ends with a rare first-person prayer, anticipating the longer prayer of chapter 23. The dunghill imagery in vv. 1-2 is deliberately coarse. Verse 9's extended meditation on grieving the fool vs. the dead is emotionally sophisticated. The "whip for thoughts" in v. 27 is striking.

---

**22:1** A sluggard is like a stone covered with filth; everyone hisses at his disgrace.

**22:2** A sluggard is like dung on a dunghill; anyone who picks it up shakes his hand clean.

**22:3** It is a father's disgrace to beget an undisciplined son; a foolish daughter is born to his loss.

**22:4** A prudent daughter will secure a husband; one who brings shame is a grief to her father.

**22:5** A shameless woman disgraces father and husband alike; she will be despised by both.

**22:6** A word at the wrong time is like music at a funeral; but rod of discipline and instruction are wisdom at every hour.

**22:7** Teaching a fool is like gluing broken pottery back together, or rousing someone from a deep sleep.

**22:8** Whoever tells something important to a fool is speaking to a drowsy man; at the end the fool will say, "What was that?"

**22:9** Weep for the dead, for the light has failed; weep for the fool, for understanding has failed. Weep more gently for the dead, for at least he has found rest; but the life of a fool is worse than death.

**22:10** The mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for a fool and a godless man it lasts all their days.

**22:11** Do not talk at length with a foolish person; do not keep company with one without understanding. Keep your distance from him, lest you have trouble, and you will not be defiled by his stumbling. Avoid him, and you will find rest; you will not grow weary in his folly.

**22:12** What is heavier than lead? And what else would you call it but "Fool"?

**22:13** Sand and salt and a lump of iron are easier to bear than a man without understanding.

**22:14** Like wooden beams bound together in a building that an earthquake cannot shake loose — so a heart established upon careful counsel holds firm.

**22:15** A thought grounded in intelligent understanding is like fine plasterwork on a smooth wall.

**22:16** Pebbles set on a height will not hold against the wind; so a cowardly heart in a fool's imagination will not hold against fear.

**22:17** A heart wounded by discernment is like a wall that has been struck — it will not stand firm against any fear.

**22:18** A heart established upon careful reflection is like smooth plasterwork on a wall.

**22:19** As pebbles thrown at birds scatter them, so reproach heaped on a friend dissolves friendship.

**22:20** Even if you drew a sword on a friend, do not despair — there is a way back. Even if you said something harsh to a friend, do not give up — reconciliation is possible. But insult and arrogance and betraying a confidence and a treacherous blow — in these a friend will flee.

**22:21** Be faithful to your neighbor in his poverty, that you may rejoice with him in his prosperity. Stand by him in his time of trouble, that you may share in his inheritance.

**22:22** Before fire come vapor and smoke from the furnace; before bloodshed come insults.

**22:23** I will not be ashamed to shelter a friend, nor hide from his face.

**22:24** And if any evil comes to me because of him, everyone who hears will guard against him.

**22:25** Who will set a guard over my mouth and a sealed lock upon my lips, that I may not fall because of them and my tongue may not destroy me?

**22:26** O LORD, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel, and do not let me fall because of them.

**22:27** Who will set a whip over my thoughts and the discipline of wisdom over my heart, to spare me nothing in my acts of folly, and not to let my sins pass unchallenged?
